Ministral3 Large costs ~1/10th of Sonnet 4.5; they clearly target different users, not a coding assistant benchmark king comparison.
A decent number of users in r/LocalLlama reported switching back from Opus 4.5 to Sonnet 4.5, suggesting trust in closed frontier providers is waning versus open alternatives like Mistral.
Mistral Large 3 is ranked 28 on LMArena, behind other SOTA models, though the ELO gap (1418 vs 1491) is relatively small, implying ~60% win rate for the leader.
Many EU companies won't risk sending data to OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google, making Mistral a real option for local/self-hosted deployment alongside Qwen and DeepSeek.
Magistral Small is a 24B parameter model performing comparably to DeepSeek V3 (671B/37B active), which is impressive in terms of efficiency for Mistral.
Benchmarks suggest Magistral loses to DeepSeek-R1 in every one-shot comparison, and likely wasn't even tested against the newer R1-0528, at more than double the cost.
Mistral's edge is speed—it answers in ~1s what takes other models 5-8s, making for a much better experience, though this speed advantage doesn't hold for web-search queries.
I am personally a fan of Mistral, because while it's not the top model, it produces good results and is super fast—it really saves a lot of time to have quick responses.
Their OCR model was hyped but on a batch of 600 page monospace PDFs, 80% of text was recognized as images and output as whitespace—much worse than tesseract. Deleted account after getting the bill.
Asked Mistral AI a Schengen immigration logic question; it initially answered incorrectly but self-corrected after being shown a Wikipedia article, doing better than Llama 4 which remained wrong.
Tested magistral-medium as a replacement for o4-mini for JSON generation where speed is critical: o4-mini took 50-70 seconds while Mistral returned results in 34-37 seconds.
Devstral (Mistral's coding model) is very useful and runs locally, according to a user testing Magistral alongside it while traveling.
Mistral OCR is super fast and significantly more accurate than Google, Claude and others for PDF to markdown conversion, priced at $1/1000 pages.
Tested Mistral OCR with a multilingual English/Hebrew bidi document—the Hebrew output had no correspondence to the source text at all, unlike its otherwise impressive benchmarks.
Found Mistral OCR much less accurate than GPT-4o on messy cursive handwriting—about 30% wrong versus closer to 5% wrong for GPT-4o.
Tried Mistral OCR with both PDFs and PNGs in Le Chat and results were the worst I've ever seen compared to Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini.
Site friction complaints: no simple sandbox to try OCR, API docs missing details on OCR endpoint and chunking behavior, notebook link is ACL'd/inaccessible.
Le Chat doesn't seem to know about the OCR change despite the blog post announcing it, making it unclear how to actually use the new OCR feature.
Wouldn't use Mistral OCR with Paperless for sensitive legal documents because of reluctance to send scans of personal documents to a third party.
